title: How it works — Green Light Buying Machine
description: Ten stages from qualification to closing, and exactly which parts we coach and which parts you own.
heading: How it works
lede: Ten stages from qualification to closing. You buy the house, run the renovation, and own every decision. We coach the process, certify the result, and list it.

blocks.heading: It's a flip. The exit is what changes.
blocks.body:
You buy the distressed house and finance it the way you always do — first, second, hard money, your usual stack. You run your crew, you hold the budget, you own the risk. Nothing about the acquisition or the buildout is unfamiliar.

What changes is who you sell to. A retail buyer prices your house against comps down the street. A co-living investor prices it against what the finished house produces by the room, and that's a different number.

The other change is where the finished house gets listed. A certified property goes into our registry and in front of buyers specifically looking for co-living assets. To be plain about it: we provide listing visibility. We don't match buyers to sellers, negotiate, or guarantee that any property sells, at any price or on any timeline.

blocks.heading: We'll teach you the way we build
blocks.lede: An investor pricing a house on room income is a different buyer than a family pricing it on comps. Almost nothing about your process changes. What you produce at the end does.

items.title: The process
items.body: Our developed standard of practice for taking a fix-and-flip operator into co-living: locating, structuring, financing, and renovating — taught in coaching, weekly the first month and every other week after.

items.title: Everything about the property
items.body: You buy it, finance it, hire and supervise your own contractors, set your own pricing, and retain full operational control. We coach; we don't manage your renovation.

items.title: Certification and listing
items.body: A documentation-based review against our standards, and listing visibility to registered buyers through the Marketplace Module. Sales happen directly between you and the buyer.

blocks.heading: The Green Light Way
blocks.body:
The floor is eight bedrooms and two bathrooms. We don't build below it, because room count is where the economics come from.

Bedrooms don't tell you what a co-living house is worth. Rentable rooms do — and not every room is worth the same. PadSplit reports what rooms actually rent for by submarket, and a room with its own ensuite bathroom prices differently than one sharing down the hall. That turns bathroom count into an underwriting decision rather than a finish preference.

It's also why we start from scratch rather than converting an existing rental. Adding bathrooms is the kind of thing you can only plan from the first wall.

blocks.heading: Financing that already understands the asset

columns.body: Rachelle Coffey is the lender we work with, and she finances PadSplit conversions specifically — both the acquisition side for operators and the purchase side for buyers.

That matters more than it sounds. A lender who prices this asset on room income rather than residential comps removes the friction that stalls these deals at the appraisal.

blocks.heading: Ten stages, start to close
blocks.lede: Every student runs the same sequence, tracked in your portal so you always know what's next and what's waiting on you.

items.title: Qualification
items.body: We confirm your experience, capital, and capacity before you enroll.

items.title: Market brief
items.body: Where co-living works, and why. We'll walk you through what to check on parking and occupancy rules city by city — confirming it stays your responsibility.

items.title: Deal sourced
items.body: We bring you a property already screened for co-living use and room count.

items.title: Room-count underwriting
items.body: Pricing a house on rentable rooms instead of bedrooms.

items.title: You buy it
items.body: Your offer, your financing, your name on the deed.

items.title: Scope and design
items.body: Floor plan, partition strategy, and finish standard.

items.title: Renovation
items.body: Your crew executes. We hand-hold to the standard and review at checkpoints.

items.title: Certification review
items.body: You submit documentation and video walkthroughs; we review them against our standards. Certification attaches to that address.

items.title: Furnish and launch
items.body: We furnish the house and get it live on PadSplit, ready to produce income on day one.

items.title: Listed and sold
items.body: Your certified property is listed for registered buyers. You negotiate and close directly with whoever buys it.

blocks.heading: $15,000 to onboard
blocks.body:
You apply first. We review your background, and if it's a fit we talk. Nothing is due before you're accepted.

The onboarding fee covers coaching, education materials, certification, and platform setup. It's non-refundable once you're in, because the digital resources open immediately.

Ongoing membership and platform fees also apply. We'll walk you through the full fee schedule during the application conversation, before you commit to anything — and it's all set out in the agreement you'd sign.

None of it includes the house. You buy and finance the property and the renovation yourself, exactly as you would any fix and flip. Membership is month to month; either side can end it with 30 days' written notice, and certification goes inactive if membership lapses.
